title: How to Call a Method in Java?

sections.heading: How to Call a Method in Java?
paragraphs: In Java, a method is a collection of statements that performs a specific task or operation. It is widely used because it provides the reusability of code means that written once and used many times. It also offers easy modification. Each method has its name by which it is called. When the compiler reads the method name, the method is called and performs the specified task.
To read more Method in Java and Types of Methods in Java

sections.heading: Calling Instance Method in Java
paragraphs: The method of the class where it is defined is known as an instance method. It is a non-static method. Before calling or invoking the instance method, it is necessary to create an object of its class. It can access the instance variables of that object. It can use this keyword to refer to the current object.

sections.heading: Calling Static Method in Java
paragraphs: In Java, a static method is a method that is invoked or called without creating an object of the class in which the method is defined. All the methods that have the static keyword before the method name are known as static methods. We can also create a static method by using the static keyword before the method name. We can call a static method by using the ClassName.methodName.
To read more Static Method in Java
The best example of the static method is the main() method. It is called without creating the object.

paragraphs: In Java, pre-defined methods are the methods that are already defined in built-in classes. When we require any pre-defined method, we just call the method by its name.

sections.heading: Calling Abstract Method in Java
paragraphs: An abstract method is a method that is declared with an abstract keyword. The abstract method only has a method declaration. The body of the abstract method is defined in the other class. The abstract method must be declared in the abstract class. We can set the visibility of abstract methods as private or public. We cannot declare an abstract method as final because it violates the advantage of the abstract method.

sections.heading: Calling Final Method in Java
paragraphs: A method declared as final is known as a final method. It cannot be overridden by the sub class. The final method can be called like any other method.

sections.heading: Calling Synchronized Method in Java
paragraphs: The synchronized keyword can be used with methods and blocks. When a method or block is declared as synchronized, a lock is obtained on the specified object, and other threads are blocked from accessing the synchronized code until the lock is released.

A synchronized method is used when we want to ensure that only one thread at a time can access the entire method. It is useful when the method modifies shared resources (like class variables or data structures).

sections.heading: Example: Calling Synchronized Method
paragraphs: We can call a synchronized method just like any other method. The difference is that the JVM ensures only one thread can execute it at a time, preventing race conditions and ensuring thread safety.
